newsitem.title: JAPAN: Key JGBs end Tokyo at 3-mth high after BOJ report.
newsitem.headline: Key JGBs end Tokyo at 3-mth high after BOJ report.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract closed at a three-month high on Thursday after the release of a central bank report showing a weak outlook for the economy.
"The report confirmed the market's recent expectation that the economic recovery may remain sluggish in the July-September period," said a dealer at a city bank's securities unit.
The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said the economic recovery was unlikely to gather significant momentum in view of fragility in some sectors as well as continued pressure from balance-sheet adjustments.

The JGB market entered a downtrend on April 25 when Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co's business was suspended, the first such case among domestic insurers in the postwar period, triggering fears of higher interest rates.
Japan's low interest rate policy had been blamed for low returns on investments.

"We had expected a change in the BOJ's current low interest rate policy in October at the earliest. But that seems less likely to happen (after Thursday's BOJ report) than before," said a market analyst at another city bank's securities unit.
But traders said initial buying after the release of the BOJ report at 2.30 p.m. (0530 GMT) stopped when profit-taking emerged at around 125.80.
"I'd like to see if investors rush to buy the newly offered 2.5 percent 10-year JGBs tomorrow," the first dealer said.

Traders said some investors had been hesitant to buy the 194th 2.5 percent 10-year issue due to its low coupon rate, but were instead buying municipal and government-guaranteed bonds as well as long-term corporate bonds.
The key 182nd 10-year JGB yield stood at 2.210 percent at 0700 GMT against Wednesday's 2.230 percent close.
So far, city banks were key buyers of the 194th issue which is unlisted at their end-September interim book closings.

Traders said the market was almost ready to rally after Wednesday's not-so-bad results of the 194th JGB auction and comments from a Japanese politician that Japan should not raise interest rates this year. Opposition New Frontier Party politician Yoshio Suzuki, who is also a former BOJ executive director, told Reuters Financial Television late on Wednesday that Japan should not raise interest rates this year, as such a move could harm the economy and financial institutions.
